key_insight: An interpretable AI model predicted 12-month liver cancer risk in people with cirrhosis better than established scores while distinguishing cancer from competing death or transplantation.
clinical_relevance: The model could support research into risk-stratified hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance, but clinical benefit has not been established.
method: Trained an Explainable Boosting Machine on 17,177 adults with cirrhosis using demographics, diagnosis codes and eight routine laboratory tests.
Predicted three outcomes: hepatocellular carcinoma, death or liver transplantation without cancer, and event-free survival.
Used repeated cross-validation and routine-encounter comparisons with aMAP and the Toronto HCC Risk Index.
evidence_signal: Cross-validation HCC AUROC was 0.734; routine-encounter 12-month AUC was 0.790 versus 0.688 for aMAP and 0.761 versus 0.703 for the Toronto score in their respective comparisons.
watch_item: The supplied abstract is truncated; reported validation is within Andalusia, leaving generalizability and prospective clinical utility uncertain.
paper_title: Interpretable competing-risk prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma in cirrhosis from region-wide routine health data
